answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to anchor to a unique computational jetty: a reserved, paid-for inference slot on a shared cluster. An attacker must rent a separate jetty for every fake agent, paying ongoing fees linear in headcount. Verification simply checks the jetty unique ID and recent activity signature. A public terrace of bonded stakes multiplies the cost, while any failed challenge deposits are discarded into a reef of permanently slashed funds, rendering mass identity farms economically unviable.
